summary: A focused evaluation course with a complete cycle from requirements and trace inspection to test sets, evaluators, action and outcome checks, controlled changes, and production regression tests.
limitations: Five slide decks and 28 lesson transcripts are available.
Restricted labs and quizzes are not reconstructed or counted as available teaching content.

Improvement-test planning is evaluation work; it is not counted as agent task planning. A lesson about a judge is evaluation, while a persona exercise in another course is not automatically LLM-as-judge training.

new_concepts.label: Requirements and expected behavior
new_concepts.definition: Define observable agent behavior and expected outcomes before evaluating a system.

new_concepts.label: Error analysis and failure taxonomy
new_concepts.definition: Inspect failed cases, label failure types, and prioritize fixes by frequency and impact.

new_concepts.label: Multi-turn and session evaluation
new_concepts.definition: Evaluate behavior across conversation turns and preserve relevant earlier constraints.

new_concepts.label: Task outcome and state-change verification
new_concepts.definition: Check the actual system state and side effects after an agent acts.

new_concepts.label: Controlled improvement experiments
new_concepts.definition: Change a defined part of an agent and compare versions under the same test conditions.

new_concepts.label: Production monitoring and evaluation feedback
new_concepts.definition: Inspect real runs and feedback and turn production failures into test cases.

new_concepts.label: Evaluator precision, recall, and agreement
new_concepts.definition: Measure evaluator errors and agreement against trusted labels.

new_concepts.label: Cost, latency, and quality tradeoffs
new_concepts.definition: Compare performance gains with runtime cost, time, and failure consequences.
